info.name: quine-erp — Organization API
info.description:
Test data and assertions for every organization endpoint (register, T5a–T5e), the login (T7b-1) and the real authentication of the tenant endpoints (T7b-2).

**Run the whole collection in order** (Collection Runner or newman). Each request stores the ids and tokens that later requests need.

**Start the application** with `docker compose up -d --build` (no profile; compose enables the tenant activation route, see below). Export `QUINE_DB_PASSWORD` and `QUINE_JWT_SECRET` first, with random values, as the README says: nothing secret is stored in this collection.

**Owners and tokens:** registering creates the tenant's owner from `ownerEmail` and `ownerPassword`. The collection generates throwaway demo values at the start of each run (collection variables `ownerPassword`, `ownerEmailA`, ...). Folder 0 ("Register then Login") registers A and B and logs both owners in: the run-time collection variables `tokenA` and `tokenB` hold the tokens (no initial value, never exported). Tenant endpoints are authenticated with `Authorization: Bearer {{tokenA}}` set at collection level; requests of tenant B override it with `{{tokenB}}`, and the requests that test a missing token or the public routes use no authorization. The tenant is read from the token's `tenantId` claim only: no header, path, query or body ever carries it.

**Activation:** organization A is activated in folder 0 through the real tenant route `POST /api/organizations/{id}/activation` with token A. That route exists only while the flag `quine.organization.tenant-activation.enabled` is `true`: docker-compose sets it, and it is `false` (route absent) by default. It is a transitional route for local and team use (T7 PO-1); it must never be enabled in an environment reachable by anyone outside the team, and T9d removes it. Without the flag, the activation requests answer 404 and every later step fails.

**Public routes:** `POST /api/organizations` and `POST /api/auth/login` need no token (and are sent with none: a stale or malformed `Authorization` header is refused even there). Every other route answers 401 `TENANT_NOT_RESOLVED` without a valid token, with the header `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="quine-erp"`.

Clients must branch on `code` only. `message` is developer-facing English (T5f).

item.description:
Registers two organizations (tenant A and tenant B), logs both owners in (stores the run-time variables `tokenA` and `tokenB`) and activates A through the real tenant route `POST /api/organizations/{id}/activation` with token A.

The activation route exists only with the flag `quine.organization.tenant-activation.enabled=true` (docker-compose sets it; default `false`, route absent). Local and team use only: see the collection description.

item.name: 1. Register organization — POST /api/organizations
item.description: Public endpoint. It never reads a tenant: registration creates the tenant.

item.name: Invalid owner e-mail and short password → 400 (pinned, no echo)

exec: pm.test("pinned messages", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("ownerEmail: must be a valid e-mail address; ownerPassword: size must be between 12 and 72"));

pm.test("pinned message", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("ownerEmail: must not be blank; ownerPassword: must not be blank"));

5. Close organization (T5d) — POST /api/organizations/{id}/closure
item.description: There is no request body. The tenant closes, with no confirmation step (PO 2026-09-28). Closing is irreversible.

item.name: 6. Activate organization (T5e) — POST /api/organizations/{id}/activation
item.description: There is no request body. The tenant activates its own organization (PO 2026-10-01). Only PENDING_ACTIVATION can be activated. Runs last: organization B is still PENDING here, and A is CLOSED.

exec: pm.test("message names the parameter", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("id: must be a valid UUID"));

item.name: 8. Authentication of tenant routes (T7b-2)
item.description: The tenant routes need a valid token. Every refusal is the same 401 `TENANT_NOT_RESOLVED` with the header exactly `Bearer realm="quine-erp"` and no detail on why. A token of tenant A never reaches tenant B's organization: the answer is the 404 of a missing organization. Runs after folder 6, so B is active (the closure requests below never reach it).

exec: pm.test("WWW-Authenticate is exactly Bearer realm=\"quine-erp\" (no error detail)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("WWW-Authenticate")).to.eql('Bearer realm="quine-erp"'));
